transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I guess what finally made me come in is that I just don’t feel like myself anymore. I used to make time for things I cared about—painting, hiking, choir, Sunday family get-togethers—and now, even if I have a free hour, I just kind of sit there. I can’t seem to care about any of it.
Have you been feeling sad or empty most of the time?

Yes. Most days it feels like there’s this heavy gray film over everything. I can be in the classroom with students, or at home with my husband, and still feel really hollow… like I’m close to tears even when nothing specific has happened.
Do you still enjoy things you used to like, or has the pleasure gone away?

The pleasure has mostly gone away. I used to really look forward to painting, hiking, singing in choir, seeing family on Sundays… and now even when I have the time, I just sit there. I can’t seem to make myself care about any of it.
Have you noticed any significant change in your weight recently?
I haven’t really noticed a big change in my weight. I don’t think my clothes are fitting much differently or anything like that.
Have you been having trouble sleeping?

Yes, definitely. My sleep has been really inconsistent for months now. I’ll lie there awake, going over grant details in my head, and then a lot of nights I wake up around three or four and can’t really get back to sleep. Even when I do sleep longer, I still wake up feeling like I didn’t rest.
Have you noticed yourself moving or speaking more slowly than usual, or feeling restless and fidgety?
I’m not really sure. I haven’t noticed myself talking slower, exactly. I do feel like I sit still a lot, but I don’t know if that’s the same thing. I’m not especially fidgety that I can tell.
Have you been having any thoughts about hurting yourself?

Yes… not in the sense that I’ve made a plan to hurt myself. But late at night, when I’m alone in the studio, I sometimes think it would be a relief if I just didn’t wake up. That scares me. I told my husband because I didn’t feel like I could keep handling those thoughts by myself.
How long have you been feeling this way?
It’s been building for about eight months now. I think it started around when I took over the STEM-Arts curriculum initiative, and it’s just… gradually gotten heavier since then.
Have you been feeling guilty or worthless about yourself or your situation?

Yes. I feel guilty a lot. If anything goes wrong with the curriculum project, even something small, I start thinking I’m letting the students down. And then it turns into this feeling that I’m wasting what my parents sacrificed for me to have the opportunities I’ve had. It’s hard to shake that.
Have you been unable to concentrate or make decisions?
I’m not sure. I mean, I have days where I feel slower or I second-guess myself, but I don’t know if I’d say I can’t concentrate or make decisions. It’s not something I’ve really been tracking.
Do you feel like you're moving slower than you used to?
I’m not really sure. I haven’t noticed myself physically moving slower, at least not in a clear way. Maybe I feel slower in my head sometimes, but I don’t know if that’s what you mean.
Do you find yourself fidgeting or restless when you're sitting or lying down?
I don’t think so. I haven’t really noticed myself fidgeting or feeling restless when I’m sitting or lying down.
Have you had any days in the past two weeks where you felt somewhat better, or has it been consistently bad?

It’s been bad most days, honestly. Maybe there are small moments where I’m distracted, but overall it feels like there’s this heavy gray film over everything. I can be in the classroom with students or at home with my husband and still feel hollow, like I’m close to crying.
Would you say that these feelings of sadness and emptiness are interfering with your daily life and relationships a lot, or is it more manageable?

It’s interfering a lot, yes. I’ve missed several teaching sessions, and I’ve been avoiding student workshops because I just can’t keep up with everything the way I used to. At home, my husband has had to take on more because I pull back from family plans, and I don’t feel safe just trying to push through it on my own.
Have you had any days in the past two weeks where you felt completely normal, without any of these sad or empty feelings?

No, I don’t think I’ve had a day that felt completely normal. Most days still have that heavy gray feeling over everything, even if I’m in class or at home with my husband. I can be doing ordinary things and still feel hollow, like I’m close to crying.
Would you say that there are any activities or situations that still bring you some joy or relief from these sad and empty feelings?

Not really. I mean, I used to make time for things I loved—painting, hiking, choir, even Sunday family gatherings. Now even if I have a free hour, I just kind of sit there. I can’t seem to care about any of it, and that’s part of what made me realize I don’t feel like myself anymore.
Would you say that your feelings of sadness and emptiness are present most of the day?

Yes. Most days it’s there for most of the day. It feels like this heavy gray film over everything, even when I’m standing in a classroom with students or just at home with my husband. I still feel hollow, and like I’m close to crying.
Would you say that your feelings of sadness and emptiness are severely impacting your ability to function in daily life?

Yes. It’s been affecting things a lot. I’ve missed several teaching sessions, and I’ve been avoiding the student workshops because I just can’t keep up with the responsibilities like I used to.

At home, my husband has had to step in more. I’ve been pulling back from family plans, and I don’t really feel safe just trying to push through it by myself.
Would you say that your feelings of sadness and emptiness are nearly constant throughout the day?

Yes, nearly. Most days it feels like it’s just there all day, like a heavy gray film over everything. Even if I’m in class with students or at home with my husband, I still feel hollow and close to tears.
Would you say that your feelings of sadness and emptiness are so severe that they are nearly constant throughout the day and interfering with almost all aspects of your life?

Yes... it feels that way most days. It’s like there’s this heavy gray film over everything. I can be in a classroom full of students, or at home with my husband, and I still feel hollow and like I’m close to crying.
